acceptance.criterion_verbatim: EC2 BUNDLES pick the stamp up at next touch (state the mechanism; no bundle rebuild is required by this TO).
acceptance.invocation: read infra/aws/ec2/safe-ec2-deploy.sh:155 + EC2_MANIFEST.json service scan + comp-find 'build_package' infra/aws/ec2
acceptance.output_evidence:
MECHANISM: the stamp is emitted by the BUILDER, never by the deploy path, so any EC2 service that adopts a build_package.py-style bundling builder inherits BUILD_MANIFEST automatically at its next build -- no bundle rebuild is required by this TO and none was performed.

MEASURED GAP, stated rather than papered over: there are NO EC2 bundles today. `infra/aws/ec2/safe-ec2-deploy.sh` is a WRAPPER -- it resolves the service from EC2_MANIFEST.json, warns on uncommitted changes, then at :155 delegates to a per-service deploy script (`bash "$DEPLOY_SCRIPT" $DEPLOY_ARGS`) and records the manifest. EC2 code ships as LOOSE OBJECTS to S3 per Rule 12, not as zip bundles (the 2026-08-18 census hashed ~460 loose code objects across 17 services with a readable staging surface). Scan: 0 of 27 EC2_MANIFEST services reference build_package; comp-find 'build_package' over infra/aws/ec2 returned 0 hits across 347 files scanned.

So the criterion's premise -- that EC2 'bundles' exist for the stamp to reach -- does not hold on the measured estate. The mechanism is correct and inert.
acceptance.denominator: 0 of 27 EC2_MANIFEST services reference a bundling builder; 0 hits across 347 files scanned under infra/aws/ec2

mutant.description: TWO-SIDED DETERMINISM CONTROL, because each side falsifies a different claim and a one-sided check would pass while the other property was broken. Rebuild each package at a FIXED pin and compare: (a) the zip sha256 must be IDENTICAL -- if built_at had leaked into the in-zip manifest it would differ, so this side falsifies 'reproducibility survived'; (b) the sidecar built_at must DIFFER -- if it were a frozen constant it would match, so this side falsifies 'the field is live rather than merely present'. A field can be present and dead; only (b) can tell.
mutant.expected: (a) identical zip sha256 across rebuilds; (b) differing sidecar built_at across rebuilds.
mutant.observed: mdpf-gold-lambda: zip sha256 1bfb547ce6ecb3aea4479147582b3d7f... == 1bfb547ce6ecb3aea4479147582b3d7f... IDENTICAL; built_at 2026-08-19T22:06:11.818410+00:00 vs 2026-08-19T22:07:25.766713+00:00 DIFFERS. opal-assets-mdpf-portal-publisher at fixed pin 4a2b34df76: zip sha256 3ee8af741807a2b50bdd39c682d8fcca... == 3ee8af741807a2b50bdd39c682d8fcca... IDENTICAL; built_at 22:08:01.670316 vs 22:08:01.992154 DIFFERS. 4/4 claims hold. ADDITIONALLY, the control FIRED A REAL FAIL first and it was isolated rather than explained away: the publisher's initial run showed differing zip hashes under `--pin HEAD`, because HEAD moved (4a2b34df76 -> 609aca9b0e) between two runs ~2 minutes apart in this shared multi-agent tree. Re-run at a fixed pin: reproducible. The control caught a genuine property of the estate, not of the change.

determinism.method: Each builder invoked twice at an identical pin; zip sha256 compared byte-wise and sidecar built_at compared for liveness. The coverage census additionally re-run at both vintages.
determinism.observed: Both homes byte-reproducible at a fixed pin (hashes above). Coverage census reproduces 0/2 complete at HEAD and 2/2 complete in the working tree across repeated runs.

surprises: `--pin HEAD` IS NOT A PIN.
